title: Splitting a zone at a block boundary
statement: Let $C$ be a type, let $row$ assign a finite list of elements of $C$ to each integer coordinate, let $j\in\mathbb Z$, and let $n,m$ be nonnegative integers. The zone of $n+m$ blocks starting at $j$ is the concatenation of the zone of $n$ blocks starting at $j$ and the zone of $m$ blocks starting at $j+n$.
hypotheses_covered: A family $row$ of lists indexed by integer coordinates
replaced:
For any family of blocks indexed by $\mathbb{Z}$ and any $j \in \mathbb{Z}$ and
$n, m \in \mathbb{N}$, the zone of $n+m$ blocks starting at $j$ is the concatenation of
the zone of $n$ blocks starting at $j$ with the zone of $m$ blocks starting at $j+n$.
